html:
The movement of workers from Kerala in south India to the oil states of the Persian Gulf, which grew into a mass migration after oil prices jumped in 1973. It is one of the largest labour flows of the late 20th century.

The oil shock of 1973 filled the treasuries of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Bahrain. They began building ports, roads, cities and hospitals and needed far more workers than they had. Kerala had old sea links to Arabia, high literacy and too few jobs, so men went in large numbers as builders, drivers, clerks, nurses and shopkeepers. Workers came from Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka too.

Most went on short contracts tied to a sponsor under the kafala system, with no path to citizenship. The money they sent home changed Kerala: new houses, private schools and hospitals, and whole villages that lived on remittances. A 2014 report found that about nine in ten of Kerala's emigrants lived in the Middle East. The chart's overlay item Gulf migration from Kerala tells the same story from the Indian side.
sum: The movement of workers from Kerala in south India to the oil states of the Persian Gulf, which grew into a mass migration after oil prices jumped in 1973. It is one of the largest labour flows of the late 20th century.
